items.raw_snippet: # From Booth to Google: An alum learns to lead AI innovation. ## Satyajeet Salgar, MBA’07, reflects on how UChicago prepared him for nearly two decades of innovation at a tech giant. *Editor’s note: This story is part of**Meet a UChicagoan**, a regular series focusing on the people who make UChicago a distinct intellectual community.*. In 2006, Satyajeet Salgar, MBA’07, was sitting in an advanced marketing class at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business when he pitched his group on a case study: a new video platform called YouTube. “The sentiment in the class was, ‘We don’t think this thing will make it to next year,’” Salgar said. In this role, Salgar leads the company’s efforts to use AI to build the next generation of products for Android, Chrome, Google Cloud, Search and more. It was a path that emerged from his graduate studies at Booth, where he learned to break a problem into its basic principles before looking for a solution.

items.raw_snippet: ## Job Type:. Working at Citi is far more than just a job. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact. We are looking for a visionary, hands-on engineering leader to build and scale the platform that will make this a reality. As the Director of Agentic Platform Engineering, you will be a player-coach responsible for the technical vision, architecture, and execution of this greenfield platform. items.snippet: **Only official editions of the Federal Register provide legal notice of publica...
items.raw_snippet: **Only official editions of the Federal Register provide legal notice of publication to the public and judicial notice to the courts under [44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2009-title44/html/USCODE-2009-title44-chap15.htm).** Learn more [here](/reader-aids/using-federalregister-gov/understanding-public-inspection). Through this succeeding notice, NIST is announcing the retitling of AISIC as the NIST Artificial Intelligence Consortium (“Consortium”), revising the scope of the Consortium's research, and reissuing its invitation to organizations to submit letters of interest in order to collaborate with NIST, non-profit organizations, industry leaders, universities, and other agencies of the Federal Government in addressing the challenges associated with the development and deployment of AI-based innovations. 116-283](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/116/public/283)), in accordance with [Executive Order 14179](/executive-order/14179) issued January 23, 2025 (Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence), and as mandated by America's AI Action Plan, issued July 2025, NIST will utilize the Consortium to empower the collaborative establishment of a new measurement science that will enable the identification of proven, scalable, and interoperable techniques and metrics to promote the development and use of AI.
